title: Tenant routing and blast radius
hook: Tenant routing directs each customer request to the correct isolated resources. Blast radius is how much damage one tenant failure or breach affects others — the core SaaS reliability and security interview topic.

blocks.text: Routing layers: DNS (tenant.app.com), API Gateway custom domain + mapping, ALB host-header rules, CloudFront alternate domain names, or application middleware resolving tenant from JWT/subdomain. Blast radius containment: separate databases, rate limits per tenant, circuit breakers, and silo tiers for critical customers. SaaS Lens Reliability and Security pillars emphasize per-tenant failure isolation.

entries.plainDefinition: Scope of impact when one component fails
entries.example: DB outage affects one tenant vs all

entries.plainDefinition: Directing request to correct tenant context
One tenant consumes disproportionate shared resources
Stop calls to failing tenant dependency

blocks.text: A bug that leaks Tenant A data to Tenant B ends careers. A noisy tenant crashing shared compute affects all customers. Interviewers want routing mechanism plus blast radius controls named explicitly.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: route by subdomain/JWT/header; contain blast radius with per-tenant limits, silo tiers, and fault isolation.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Resolve tenant identity
items.body: Subdomain, custom domain, JWT claim, or API key maps to tenant_id.

items.title: Route to correct stack
items.body: ALB rule, Lambda authorizer, or router service for silo vs pool tier.

items.title: Enforce per-tenant limits
items.body: API Gateway usage plan, WAF rate limit keyed on tenant, SQS per-tenant queues.

items.title: Contain failures
items.body: Bulkhead pattern: separate connection pools, timeouts, circuit breakers per tenant.

snippet.label: ALB host-header routing
snippet.code:
ListenerRule:
  Properties:
    Conditions:
      - Field: host-header
        Values: ['acme.app.example.com']
    Actions:
      - Type: forward
        TargetGroupArn: !Ref AcmeSiloTargetGroup
snippet.explanation: Enterprise silo tenant gets dedicated target group.

snippet.label: JWT tenant claim resolution
snippet.explanation: Cognito custom attribute or OIDC claim carries tenant identity.

snippet.label: API Gateway usage plan per tier
snippet.code:
PremiumPlan:
  Type: AWS::ApiGateway::UsagePlan
  Properties:
    UsagePlanName: premium-tier
    Throttle:
      RateLimit: 1000
      BurstLimit: 2000
    Quota:
      Limit: 1000000
      Period: MONTH
snippet.explanation: Different rate limits per SaaS tier — fairness control.

snippet.label: Per-tenant circuit breaker
snippet.explanation: One tenant bad webhook does not trip breaker for all tenants.

blocks.title: Cloud vs app patterns
rows: One bad npm dep crashes all tenants

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Tenant ID only in URL path — attacker changes path to access other tenant. Shared rate limit bucket for all tenants. No silo path for enterprise despite SLA.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: chaos test kills one tenant silo — others unaffected; pen test cross-tenant access fails; per-tenant p99 tracked separately.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Higher cost for affected tier only

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Tenant ID from client body without auth validation — rejected as insecure. Strong answer: signed JWT claim or verified subdomain mapping.

interviewTakeaways: Route tenants via subdomain, custom domain, or signed JWT claim.
Blast radius: silo tiers, per-tenant limits, circuit breakers, bulkheads.
Never trust client-supplied tenant_id without authentication.
60s: Resolve tenant from subdomain/JWT. Route pool vs silo. Per-tenant rate limits and circuit breakers. Chaos test proves isolation.
Follow-up: what if one tenant DDoSes your shared ALB?
commonPitfalls: tenant_id from query string without auth — cross-tenant access vulnerability.
Strong answer: signed claim, middleware enforcement, integration tests.
Shared rate limit — one tenant blocks all.
No silo escalation path when enterprise signs.
